Architectural Symbolism
The placement and style of carvings are
deeply tied to the temple's architectural
layout, which is designed to represent the
cosmic order.
• Cosmic Geography: The temple often
mimics Mount Meru, the axis mundi
connecting heaven and earth, with the
innermost sanctum (garbhagriha) acting
as the peak.
Narrative Progression: As devotees move
from the periphery toward the sanctum,
the carvings guide them through a
symbolic journey from the material realm
to spiritual enlightenment.
• Iconography: Deities are carved with
specific attributes, hand gestures
(mudras), and postures that convey their
unique roles, such as Shiva's dance or the
protective stance of various goddesses.
